source.title: Symmetry & critical points for a model shallow neural network

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes critical points and population squared loss in a shallow ReLU teacher-student model. It does not measure training classification error, gradient-descent outcomes from random initialization, or any other behavior named by V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports distinct spurious-minimum families and their population squared-loss values. These results do not measure the training-error or training-dynamics outcomes in the listed versions; the loss rows are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. It also cites results from Safran and Shamir, which are not recorded as this paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The study derives population losses and critical-point structure in the teacher-student model underlying V2, but does not test how gradient-descent failure frequency changes with width or extra student neurons. Section 7.5 additionally reports convergence from random initialization restricted to a symmetry-fixed subspace at k=6; this does not establish V2's standard-initialization width comparison. The other versions concern architectures, measures or training interventions not studied here.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors construct convergent power-series descriptions of critical-point families and a path-based approximation through a linear-model limit. They derive inverse-width loss decay for type II and positive limiting losses for types A and I. Hessian-based proofs of local-minimum status are attributed to companion work; type-M decay and its status for all k≥9 remain numerical or conjectural.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes a Gaussian-input, two-layer ReLU teacher-student population objective using symmetry and analytic methods; it does not test the training recipes in V1–V6.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported objective-value behavior depends on the critical-point family: type II decays with width, while types A and I approach a positive limit.

fits_no_version.finding: Type-II critical-point loss decays as (1/2−2/π²)/k, whereas types A and I approach 1/2−1/π. These are analytical critical-point values, not frequencies of optimization outcomes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different spurious-minimum families in the Gaussian-input, identity-teacher ReLU model have different asymptotic population losses as teacher and student grow together.

fits_no_version.finding: Type-M loss is approximately 5.922×10⁻⁵ at k=10⁴; numerical data suggest approximately 0.6/k decay. Its spurious-minimum status for all k≥9 remains conjectural.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Type-M critical-point losses appear to decay inversely with width over the reported numerical range.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 7.5 reports that random initialization within M(6,6) fixed by ΔS5 leads gradient descent with approximately equal probability to the global solution or each of three other critical-point families. No trial count or initialization distribution is supplied there, and no width or extra-neuron comparison is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricting initialization and gradient descent to the specified symmetry-fixed subspace can yield several distinct optimization outcomes at k=6.

record.problems: The central reported quantities are population squared objective values at critical points, not training classification error or observed training runs from random initialization. The type-M decay is described as a strong suggestion, and its status as a spurious minimum is conjectured in the cited passage.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Cited Safran and Shamir results are not this paper's own results.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, corrupted labels, convolutional-network size and training recipes.

Gradient-descent failure frequency from standard initialization as teacher and student widths grow together, and changes from adding one or two student neurons. The reported restricted-subspace experiment supplies neither comparison.
Training degradation with depth and prevention by identity shortcuts; deep plain tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Effects of initialization on learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature changes and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says no gradient-descent outcomes are reported: Section 7.5 contains the restricted-subspace experiment described above. This correction does not supply V2's standard-initialization or width comparisons. Safran and Shamir's reported failure frequencies and over-specification effects are cited results, not this study's own tests.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification error, random initialization, label corruption, model size, optimizer and training duration.
Gradient-descent termination frequency as teacher and student widths grow together, and the effect of giving the student extra neurons.
Depth, identity shortcuts and training error in plain versus residual networks.
Initialization comparisons, training speed and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss trajectories and sharpness.
Batch-normalization comparisons, training speed and learning-rate tolerance; Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: type II critical points
rows.size_stated: k neurons and k inputs; k ≥ 6 for the stated type-II spurious-minimum result
rows.operation_detail: Analyzes the objective value at the type-II critical point as k grows.
rows.note: This is expected population squared loss at a critical point, not training classification error or a reported gradient-descent outcome.
rows.check: The value agrees with Theorem 8.5. Loss at an analytically characterized critical point does not measure gradient-descent failure frequency or the benefit of extra student neurons.

rows.subject: type A critical points
rows.size_stated: k neurons and k inputs; k ≥ 6 for the stated spurious-minimum result
rows.operation_detail: Reports the limiting objective value at type-A critical points.
rows.note: This is expected population squared loss at a critical point, not training classification error or a reported gradient-descent outcome.
rows.check: The asymptotic value agrees with Proposition 8.15, but does not measure any version's training outcome.

rows.subject: type I critical points
rows.size_stated: k neurons and k inputs; k ≥ 6 for the stated spurious-minimum result
rows.operation_detail: Reports the limiting objective value at type-I critical points.
rows.note: This is expected population squared loss at a critical point, not training classification error or a reported gradient-descent outcome.
rows.check: The asymptotic value agrees with Proposition 8.15. Qualify the stated spurious-minimum threshold: the introduction specifies k≥7 for type I, and Section 9.1 repeats that qualification, although other passages say k≥6. The loss calculation itself does not establish V2's optimization-frequency comparison.

rows.subject: type M critical points
rows.size_stated: k neurons and k inputs; example at k = 10⁴
rows.operation_detail: Reports a numerical objective value and an approximate asymptotic decay for type-M critical points.

conditions.value: k = 10⁴ example; trend discussed for k ∈ [9, 20000]

rows.value: For k = 10⁴, F(c) ≈ 5.922 × 10⁻⁵; decay is strongly suggested to be approximately 0.6k⁻¹.
rows.note: The decay is described as strongly suggested, and the authors say they conjecture these critical points define spurious minima for all k ≥ 9. This is population squared loss, not training classification error or a reported gradient-descent outcome.
rows.check: The numerical value and suggested decay agree with Remark 7.6. The explicit conjecture that these are spurious minima for every k≥9 appears in Section 9.2, which should be added to the locator. Neither the numerical loss nor the conjecture measures a claimed training behavior.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
